rows.label: Residence test
rows.value: Resident with 183 days or more in Ireland in the tax year, or 280 days over the tax year and the year before taken together (not resident with 30 days or fewer in the year); any part of a day counts
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: How to know if you are resident for tax purposes (published 24 November 2025)

rows.label: Days in the tax year that make a person resident
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: How to know if you are resident for tax purposes (published 24 November 2025)

rows.label: Days over the tax year and the year before that make a person resident
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: How to know if you are resident for tax purposes (published 24 November 2025)

rows.label: Not resident when present for this many days or fewer in the tax year
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: How to know if you are resident for tax purposes (published 24 November 2025)

rows.label: What a non-resident pays income tax on
rows.value: Irish income, including pay for an employment performed in Ireland (for a person who is neither ordinarily resident nor domiciled in Ireland)
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: Tax and tax credits for non-residents (published 26 January 2026)

rows.label: How it is collected
rows.value: Through PAYE: pay for duties performed in Ireland is within the PAYE system whatever the residence of the employee or the employer (foreign employers included)
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 42-04-65, PAYE: Employee payroll tax deductions in relation to non-Irish employments exercised in the State, chapter 4 (last reviewed May 2026)

rows.label: Tax credits: EU citizens get full credits when the share of worldwide income taxable in Ireland is at least
rows.note: below it, a share of the credits in proportion to Irish income
rows.source_title: Revenue: Tax and tax credits for non-residents (published 26 January 2026)

rows.label: Tax credits: other non-residents
rows.value: Citizens of a country with a tax treaty with Ireland: full credits if their only income is Irish, otherwise a share; all other non-residents: no tax credits
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: Tax and tax credits for non-residents (published 26 January 2026)

rows.label: Short business visits: workdays in a tax year without PAYE, any country
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 42-04-65, PAYE: Employee payroll tax deductions in relation to non-Irish employments exercised in the State, chapter 4 (last reviewed May 2026)

rows.label: Short business visits: workdays without PAYE for residents of a treaty country (treaty employment article met)
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 42-04-65, PAYE: Employee payroll tax deductions in relation to non-Irish employments exercised in the State, chapter 4 (last reviewed May 2026)

rows.label: Short business visits: longer stays
rows.value: From a treaty country, up to 183 days without PAYE where Revenue has issued a PAYE dispensation; beyond the limits PAYE applies from the first workday
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 42-04-65, PAYE: Employee payroll tax deductions in relation to non-Irish employments exercised in the State, chapter 4 (last reviewed May 2026)

rows.label: Working abroad for an Irish employer (PAYE Exclusion Order)
rows.value: Revenue can authorise the employer not to deduct income tax and USC while the employee is non-resident and all duties are carried out abroad; not normally issued for non-resident directors of Irish companies
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: What is a PAYE Exclusion Order? (published 24 November 2025); PAYE Exclusion Order issued by Revenue: Non-resident directors and employees recruited abroad (published 06 November 2026); Tax and Duty Manual Part 42-04-01 (Section 984 TCA 1997)

rows.label: Split-year treatment in the year of arrival
rows.value: Employment income earned abroad before arrival is ignored, if the person is resident in the arrival year and the following year but was not resident the year before; employment income only
rows.note: Double taxation agreements can relieve a non-resident's Irish employment income; Revenue reviews the employment article of the treaty in each case. A person who arrives intending to stay can also elect to be resident in the year of arrival.
rows.source_title: Revenue: Split-year treatment in your year of arrival (published 20 January 2026)

rows.section: Contractors: employment status, RCT and PSWT
rows.label: Official test: employee or self-employed
rows.value: The five-step framework of the Supreme Court judgment of 20 October 2023 (Revenue Commissioners v Karshan (Midlands) Ltd t/a Domino's Pizza): pay for work, personal service, control, then the whole of the arrangement, then any special legislation; if any of the first three fails, there is no employment
rows.note: Wrongly treating an employee as a subcontractor leaves the business liable for the PAYE, PRSI and USC it should have deducted, with interest and penalties.
rows.source_title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 05-01-30, Revenue Guidelines for Determining Employment Status for Taxation Purposes (last reviewed May 2026); Department of Social Protection: Code of Practice on Determining Employment Status (last updated 12 May 2025); Revenue: RCT for principal contractors (published 19 May 2026)

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Corporation tax [national]
rows.value: 12.5% on trading income; 25% on non-trading income and excepted trades; 15% minimum effective rate (domestic top-up tax) for groups and standalone entities with revenue over €750,000,000. Paid by companies resident in Ireland, and non-resident companies trading through an Irish branch or agency. Taxes Consolidation Act 1997; Part 4A for the top-up taxes.
rows.note: This list covers corporate tax, self-employment and contractor rules, non-resident pay and property taxes; income tax, USC, PRSI and VAT are in the sections above. Each row has its own official source.
rows.source_title: Revenue: Corporation Tax (CT), Basis of charge (published 16 October 2026); Corporation Tax (CT), Overview (published 16 October 2026)

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Tax on distributed profits and branch profits [national]
rows.value: branch profits: corporation tax at the same rates; distributions: 25% Dividend Withholding Tax; close companies: 20% surcharge on undistributed investment and estate income (15% on half of professional and service income). Paid by companies (DWT is withheld from the shareholder's dividend). Taxes Consolidation Act 1997 Part 6 Chapter 8A (DWT), sections 440 and 441 (surcharges).
rows.note: This list covers corporate tax, self-employment and contractor rules, non-resident pay and property taxes; income tax, USC, PRSI and VAT are in the sections above. Each row has its own official source.

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Self-employed contributions: PRSI Class S [national]
rows.value: 4.2% to 30 September 2026, 4.35% from 1 October 2026 (4.2375% for 2026 income in self-assessment), minimum €650. Paid by self-employed people with income of €5,000 or more. Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005, Part 2 Chapter 3. In force from 1 January 2026.
rows.note: This list covers corporate tax, self-employment and contractor rules, non-resident pay and property taxes; income tax, USC, PRSI and VAT are in the sections above. Each row has its own official source.

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Relevant Contracts Tax (RCT) [national]
rows.value: 0%, 20% or 35% withheld, by the subcontractor's tax compliance record. Paid by subcontractors in construction, forestry and meat processing (withheld by principal contractors). Taxes Consolidation Act 1997 sections 530 to 530V.
rows.note: This list covers corporate tax, self-employment and contractor rules, non-resident pay and property taxes; income tax, USC, PRSI and VAT are in the sections above. Each row has its own official source.

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Professional Services Withholding Tax (PSWT) [national]
rows.value: 20% withheld from fees. Paid by providers of professional services to state and semi-state bodies (withheld by the payer). Taxes Consolidation Act 1997 Part 18 Chapter 1.
rows.note: This list covers corporate tax, self-employment and contractor rules, non-resident pay and property taxes; income tax, USC, PRSI and VAT are in the sections above. Each row has its own official source.

rows.label: Contractor or employee: employment status test [national]
rows.value: five-step framework from the Supreme Court judgment in the Karshan case (20 October 2023). Paid by businesses engaging workers (decides whether PAYE, PRSI and USC must be deducted). Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 05-01-30; Code of Practice on Determining Employment Status (revised November 2024).

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Simplified regimes: VAT SME scheme, moneys-received basis and flat-rate farmers [national]
rows.value: no VAT registration below €42,500 (services) or €85,000 (goods) of turnover; VAT on cash received up to €2,000,000 turnover; flat-rate addition of 4.5% for unregistered farmers. Paid by small businesses and farmers that use them. Value-Added Tax Consolidation Act 2010.

rows.section: Taxes and charges: corporate, contractor, non-resident and property
rows.label: Non-resident tax on employment income [national]
rows.value: income tax at the normal rates, collected through PAYE, on pay for duties performed in Ireland; tax credits in full or in part only for EU citizens and treaty-country citizens. Paid by non-resident employees (withheld by the employer, including foreign employers). Taxes Consolidation Act 1997 section 819 (residence), sections 984 and 985C to 985F (PAYE). In force from 1 January 2020.

rows.label: Local Property Tax [national, varied locally]
rows.value: €95 to €3,110 a year by valuation band up to €2,100,000, rates of 0.0906% to 0.3% above; local authorities vary the basic rate by up to +25% or -15%. Paid by owners of residential property. Finance (Local Property Tax) Act 2012, sections 17 and 20. In force from 1 January 2026.

rows.value: residential: 1% up to €1,000,000, 2% up to €1,500,000, 6% above; 15% on 10 or more houses in 12 months; non-residential: 7.5%. Paid by the purchaser or transferee. Stamp Duties Consolidation Act 1999, Schedule 1 and section 31E. In force from 2 October 2024.
